title: DRC Opens 2026-27 School Year Under Ebola Health Protocols; Beni Reopening Disrupted by Teacher Strike
detail: The Democratic Republic of Congo's Ministry of Education proceeded with the nationwide start of the 2026-27 school year on Tuesday, 1 September 2026, maintaining classes even in Ebola-affected zones under a 'differentiated' plan announced 19 August: green zones (unaffected) operate normally, orange zones (affected) add health screening, and 18 of 138 educational subdivisions (13%) classified red/high-risk switch temporarily to distance learning via printed materials and radio broadcasts rather than closing outright. In Beni, North Kivu — one of the hardest-hit health zones, with a roughly 69% case fatality rate — the reopening was muted: most public schools stayed shut after the Intersyndicate of Teachers (Nord-Kivu II) called a strike citing Ebola risk, unpaid health-mutual contributions (MESP), and insecurity, while a nationwide teachers' union separately began a 1-12 September strike demanding a $500 minimum salary. The few schools that opened installed hand-washing stations and thermal scanners at entrances per the North Kivu governor's directive. Parent Joël Kambale said, 'I want my child to come home healthy. I don't want school to be a contamination site,' while student Angelani Audrey said, 'We're somewhat afraid, we're here without knowing what tomorrow will be.' In Ituri province, the outbreak's epicenter, teachers reported for duty but classrooms were nearly empty, with roughly one-tenth of children attending.

title: UN Relief Chief Warns 'Time Is Not on Our Side' as Ebola Funding Gap Hits $1.1 Billion
detail: UN Emergency Relief Coordinator Tom Fletcher told reporters on 1 September 2026 that the Ebola response in DRC 'is growing and has been scaled up, but the virus is moving faster,' warning that 'time is not on our side.' He said the outbreak had reached 6,100 confirmed cases and 2,950 deaths by the prior Monday (31 August), up from 5,515 cases and 2,642 deaths at the 100-day mark, and noted more than 5,000 cases have occurred in Ituri province alone. Fletcher said a $1.1 billion funding gap remains against the response plan and called the crisis 'a humanitarian emergency layered onto many existing humanitarian emergencies,' adding 'we have beaten Ebola before, and we can do it again.' The same day, WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus addressed a High-Level Member States briefing on the DRC Ebola response, urging accelerated international funding and support.

title: CDC MMWR Report Finds DRC Ebola Response Missing Nearly All Operational Targets
detail: A CDC Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report (MMWR) 'Notes from the Field' published 1 September 2026, using data through mid-August, found the DRC's Bundibugyo virus response falling short of nearly every operational benchmark: contact tracing identified only 10.6 contacts per case versus a target of 20 or more, with just 15-20% of new cases coming from already-known contact lists; laboratory testing was completed for only 72% of suspected-case alerts against a 90% target; an estimated 59% of confirmed deaths occurred outside treatment units, indicating insufficient isolation capacity; and fewer than half of affected health zones (49%) had functioning safe-burial teams versus a 100% target. As of the mid-August data cutoff, the report recorded 5,458 confirmed cases and 2,606 deaths (48% case fatality rate), already the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record. CDC concluded that persistent gaps in surveillance, case detection, contact tracing, and funeral management are allowing the epidemic to keep spreading across DRC's six affected provinces.

sources.name: CDC MMWR — Notes from the Field: Characteristics and Monitoring of the 2026 Outbreak of Ebola Disease Caused by Bundibugyo Virus, DRC
